_meta.method: Web search plus direct fetches of primary pages, statutes, tariff APIs and PDFs. 'confirmed' is true only when the figure was read on the cited page or document itself during this session. Where a figure was seen only in a search-engine excerpt, or the page blocked retrieval, confirmed is false and the note says so. Nothing here is invented; unpublished values are null with a note.

deficiency.text: Under the UCC the debtor stays liable for any deficiency after a commercially reasonable disposition (UCC § 9-615(d)); state consumer statutes can bar it (see below).

faaRegistry.text: The repossessor files FAA Form 8050-4 (Certificate of Repossession of Encumbered Aircraft), the security agreement if not already recorded, and, when repossession ended in a foreclosure sale, a bill of sale signed by the sheriff or auctioneer, with a new registration application and fee.
faaRegistry.note: Content from search excerpts of the FAA/eCFR pages; not fetched in full. Liens are recorded at the FAA Aircraft Registry under 49 U.S.C. chapter 441.

california.text: The Unruh Act (Civil Code 1801 et seq.) 'shall not apply to any contract... for the sale of any aircraft required to be registered under the Federal Aviation Act of 1958'. Rees-Levering covers only vehicles registered under the Vehicle Code. So a California aircraft loan falls back on UCC Article 9, and the Unruh anti-deficiency rule (Civil Code 1812.5) does not reach it.
california.note: The same section excludes vessels whose cash price exceeds $25,000.

connecticut.coversAircraft: yes, if bought primarily for personal use with an aggregate cash price of $75,000 or less
connecticut.text: The Retail Installment Sales Financing Act defines 'goods' as consumer goods up to $75,000 aggregate cash price (equipment up to $25,000), and covers both seller-financed contracts and 'installment loan contracts' (a loan to pay the purchase price, secured by the goods). Self-help only without breach of the peace; optional 10-day notice of intent to repossess; if no notice, a 15-day redemption period and a statement within 3 days; compulsory resale 15 to 180 days after retaking with at least 10 days' written notice; proceeds credited at the greater of sale price or fair retail market value. Deficiency is barred except for motor vehicles and boats over $4,000 cash price, so an aircraft under this act carries no deficiency.
connecticut.note: The no-deficiency reading for aircraft is our reading of the statute's text; no case law checked. Most aircraft cost more than $75,000 and fall outside the act.

newYork.coversAircraft: only seller-financed retail instalment contracts, not bank loans
newYork.text: Personal Property Law art. 10 (Retail Instalment Sales Act) defines 'goods' as all personal chattels sold for other than commercial or business use, excluding motor vehicles covered by articles 9 and 9-A. An aircraft bought for personal use on a seller's instalment contract is 'goods'; a direct loan from a bank is not a retail instalment contract. Neither article bars a deficiency, so UCC Article 9 governs enforcement.
newYork.note: The definition was confirmed; the conclusion about deficiency and bank loans is our inference and was not checked against case law.

intoCanada.duty: Outboard motorboats not over 7.5 m are tariff item 8903.93.90: MFN 9.5%, United States Tariff (UST) and Mexico Tariff Free, UK Tariff Free. A US-origin boat qualifying under CUSMA enters free; a non-originating boat pays 9.5%.
intoCanada.publisher: Canada Border Services Agency, Customs Tariff chapter 89 (2026)
intoCanada.gst: 5% GST on value plus duty (CBSA duties-and-taxes guide, modified 2026-09-17, https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/import/guide-3-eng.html, primary, confirmed through its worked example).

hst.text: For a personal import into a participating province, CBSA collects HST (Ontario 13%) instead of GST alone.
hst.note: Standard CBSA practice; not read on a page this session.

intoCanada.luxuryTax: Vessels with a taxable amount over CAD 250,000 bear the Select Luxury Items Tax since 2022-09-01 (CBSA, https://www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca/import/imp-mar-eng.html, modified 2022-08-29, primary, confirmed).
intoCanada.reporting: Declare the boat to CBSA on first arrival and pay duty and taxes; by water, report at a designated marine site and call the Telephone Reporting Centre, 1-888-226-7277 (CBSA, primary; phone number from a search excerpt).

transportCanada.text: Pleasure craft up to 24 m must meet the construction standards in force when built or imported and carry a compliance notice; Transport Canada says a vessel imported for personal use (not under contract or for resale) may not need one, with other exceptions in Part 8 of the Small Vessel Regulations. A powered boat must also be licensed (pleasure craft licence through Transport Canada) or registered.
transportCanada.note: The personal-use exemption came from a search excerpt of this TC page; our fetch of the page did not show it. No import inspection fee by Transport Canada was found.

intoCanada.trailer: A trailer imported with the boat goes through the Registrar of Imported Vehicles (RIV) if under 15 years old; a fee of about CAD 295 is reported (BorderBuddy, secondary, not confirmed).

intoUnitedStates.duty: HTS 8903.93.20 outboard motorboats not over 7.5 m: general 1%, column 2 30%, special Free for programs including 'S' (USMCA), so a USMCA-originating boat from Canada enters duty-free (General Note 11).
intoUnitedStates.publisher: US International Trade Commission, Harmonized Tariff Schedule
intoUnitedStates.note: The 1.5% rate often quoted applies to motorboats other than outboard (and some other lines); the 2.7% line 8903.93.15 covers other small craft. USMCA treatment for Canadian-built boats needs origin qualification. Separate 2025 US additional duties on non-USMCA Canadian goods may apply; not checked for boats.
intoUnitedStates.requirements: Report to CBP on arrival; formal vessel entry on CBP Form 1300 within 48 hours when arriving by water; proof of ownership; EPA engine declaration Form 3520-21; Coast Guard Notice of Arrival where required (secondary sources: GHY International, Waggoner Guide; not confirmed on cbp.gov).

merchandiseProcessingFee.note: Formal entries carry the ad valorem MPF with a minimum and maximum; FY2026 figures not checked.

importUK.duty: UK Global Tariff: third-country duty 0.00% on pleasure motorboats (8903 93 90 00 and 8903 31 00 00); 35% additional duty on Russian or Belarusian origin.
importUK.publisher: HM Revenue & Customs, UK Trade Tariff
importUK.note: Relief: Temporary Admission for non-UK-resident owners, normally up to 24 months in Great Britain or 18 months in Northern Ireland (secondary).

importIreland.duty: EU third-country duty 1.70% on 8903 93 90 (outboard motorboats not over 7.5 m) for US origin; no additional US-specific measure shown for 2026-09-30. UK-originating boats enter free under the EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement if origin is proved.

vat.basis: customs value plus duty and costs to the point of entry
vat.note: Ireland's standard VAT rate; not read on revenue.ie this session.

importIreland.temporaryAdmission: Non-EU-resident pleasure boats may enter without duty or VAT and must be re-exported within 18 months (Revenue, https://www.revenue.ie/en/customs/individuals/boats-aircraft/index.aspx, primary, confirmed).
importIreland.note: An EU resident bringing in a non-EU boat pays VAT at once. Irish pleasure boats pay no VRT; not checked this session.

primaryDataset.name: DVSA 'Anonymised MOT tests and results' bulk dataset
primaryDataset.note: DVSA's own published age table we found (dvsa-com-05, 'vehicle initial test fail rate by age') covers HGVs, trailers and buses, not cars. Car figures by age come from third-party analyses of the bulk data.

analyses.extra: Search excerpts from the same publisher: failure peaks at 42.7% at 18–21 years and falls to 33.3% at 27–30 years, because neglected cars have been scrapped (not confirmed on the page).
analyses.note: Fail percentages are 100 minus the published pass rate.

analyses.measure: initial failure rate (at least one failing defect), class 4 cars, 33,012,215 tests
analyses.overall: 28.28% of initial tests found at least one failing defect; 22.8% strict fail rate after defects fixed at the test station
analyses.note: Only the endpoints were quoted on the page; per-year values sit in the CSVs at https://github.com/ivitskiy/uk-mot-risk-index-dataset (CC BY 4.0).

motByAge.note: The three analyses define failure differently (strict fail, fail including defects fixed during the test, cohort-averaged), so their numbers do not agree exactly. The pattern agrees: about 11–14% at the first MOT, about 23–32% at ten years, about 40–44% near 18–20 years. RAC, Autotrader and BookMyGarage age tables were not found.
